history.summary: NOTE: the famous Rani Sati Temple stands at Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan; THIS is a smaller shrine in Sector 16-17, Hisar (house 649-650, ~4.6 rating on listing sites) venerating the same deity - its founding date and history are UNVERIFIED in web sources, treated here as a contemporary shrine. The deity's legend: Narayani Devi of Dokwa (Rajasthan), wife of Tandhan of Hisar, avenged her husband's death at the hands of the king of Hisar and then immolated herself on his pyre; Ranaji the horse-keeper arranged the pyre and was blessed that his name would be taken before hers. Dating of the event varies in retellings (1295 / 14th century / 1595 / 17th century).

name: Rani Sati Temple
town_description: Hisar is a city in northwestern Haryana founded in 1354 as Hisar-e-Firoza by Firoz Shah Tughlaq. It is a major agricultural and industrial hub (notably steel) and an important rail junction in the state. The city and its surroundings have deep archaeological roots, with sites linked to the Indus Valley and early historic periods.
tradition: Hinduism (folk/Shakti worship of Rani Sati Dadi)
